content.definition: Creditor grants concession to debtor experiencing financial difficulties
two_conditions_required: 2. Creditor grants a concession (wouldn't otherwise grant)

settlement_of_debt.description: Debtor transfers assets or equity to creditor in full settlement of debt

debtor_accounting.gain_on_restructuring: Carrying amount of debt - FV of assets/equity transferred
debtor_accounting.gain_loss_on_asset: FV of asset transferred - carrying amount of asset
debtor_accounting.two_gains_possible: Gain on asset disposal AND gain on restructuring

creditor_accounting.loss: Carrying amount of receivable - FV of assets/equity received

modification_of_terms.description: Change debt terms (reduce principal, reduce interest rate, extend maturity)

debtor_accounting.test: Compare carrying amount of debt to total FUTURE CASH PAYMENTS (principal + interest)
debtor_accounting.if_future_payments_greater: NO gain. Use effective interest method going forward (discount future payments at new rate).
debtor_accounting.if_future_payments_less: Recognize GAIN immediately = Carrying amount - Total future payments. NO interest expense in future (all payments reduce principal).

creditor_accounting.impairment: If present value of future cash flows < carrying amount, recognize impairment loss
creditor_accounting.discount_rate: Use original effective rate (not new rate) to calculate PV

debtor_accounting_settlement.step_1: Adjust asset to fair value, recognize gain/loss on asset
debtor_accounting_settlement.step_2: Remove debt, recognize gain on debt restructuring

example.step_1_asset: Gain on asset = $85K - $70K = $15K. DR Asset $15K, CR Gain on Asset $15K
example.step_2_debt: Gain on restructuring = $100K - $85K = $15K. DR Debt $100K, CR Asset $85K, CR Gain on Restructuring $15K

scenario_1_future_payments_greater.facts: Debt $100K (includes $10K accrued interest). Terms changed: Reduce principal to $90K, extend maturity, new rate 5% for 5 years. Total future payments: $90K principal + $22.5K interest = $112.5K.
scenario_1_future_payments_greater.accounting: NO gain recognized. Use effective interest method. Calculate new effective rate to discount $112.5K to $100K over 5 years.

scenario_2_future_payments_less.facts: Debt $100K. Terms changed: Reduce principal to $80K, no interest, due in 5 years. Total future payments: $80K.
scenario_2_future_payments_less.accounting: Gain = $100K - $80K = $20K. DR Debt $20K, CR Gain on Restructuring $20K. NO interest expense in future (all $80K payment reduces principal).

creditor_accounting_settlement.loss_calculation: Carrying amount of receivable - FV of assets received

example.entry: DR Asset $85K, DR Loss on Restructuring $15K, CR Receivable $100K

creditor_accounting_modification.impairment_test: Calculate present value of future cash flows using ORIGINAL effective rate
creditor_accounting_modification.if_impaired: Recognize impairment loss = Carrying amount - PV of future cash flows

example.facts: Receivable $100K, original effective rate 10%. New terms: $80K due in 5 years, no interest.
example.impairment: $100K - $49.7K = $50.3K loss. DR Impairment Loss $50.3K, CR Allowance $50.3K

no_gain_or_loss_scenario.when: Present value of future cash flows (using new effective rate) approximately equals carrying amount
no_gain_or_loss_scenario.accounting: Simply adjust debt to new terms, use new effective interest rate going forward

settlement.debtor: Gain = CA of debt - FV transferred. Plus gain/loss on asset disposal.
settlement.creditor: Loss = CA of receivable - FV received.

modification.debtor: If total future payments < CA: Recognize gain, no future interest. If future payments > CA: No gain, use effective interest.
modification.creditor: Impairment = CA - PV of future cash flows (discounted at ORIGINAL rate).

calculation_example_complex.facts: Debtor owes $100K plus $5K accrued interest = $105K total. Debtor transfers asset (BV $60K, FV $80K).
debtor_entries: Step 1 - Adjust asset to FV: DR Asset $20K, CR Gain on Asset $20K
Step 2 - Settle debt: DR Note Payable $100K, DR Interest Payable $5K, CR Asset $80K, CR Gain on Restructuring $25K
calculation_example_complex.creditor_entry: DR Asset $80K, DR Loss on Restructuring $25K, CR Note Receivable $105K

cpa_exam_tips: Settlement: Debtor recognizes TWO gains (asset disposal + restructuring). Creditor recognizes loss.
Modification: Debtor compares CA to TOTAL FUTURE CASH PAYMENTS (not PV).
If future payments < CA: Debtor recognizes gain immediately, NO interest expense in future
If future payments > CA: NO gain, use effective interest method
Creditor: Calculate impairment using PV of future cash flows at ORIGINAL effective rate

debtor_settlement_steps: 1. Adjust asset to FV, recognize gain/loss on asset
2. Remove debt, record asset at FV, recognize gain on restructuring (CA of debt - FV of asset)
debtor_modification_steps: 1. Calculate total future cash payments (principal + all interest)
2. Compare to carrying amount of debt
3. If future < CA: Gain = CA - future payments. No future interest expense.
4. If future > CA: No gain. Use effective interest method.
cpa_exam_strategies.creditor_modification: Calculate PV of future cash flows using ORIGINAL rate. Impairment = CA - PV.
common_mistakes: For debtor modification: Using PV instead of total future cash payments for gain test
Forgetting to recognize gain on asset disposal in settlement (recognizing only restructuring gain)
For creditor modification: Using new rate instead of original rate to calculate PV
Recognizing interest expense when future payments < CA (should have no interest expense)

key_points: Troubled debt restructuring: Debtor in financial difficulty + Creditor grants concession
Settlement: Debtor recognizes gain on asset disposal AND gain on restructuring. Creditor recognizes loss.
Modification - Debtor: Compare CA to total future cash payments. If future < CA: Gain, no future interest. If future > CA: No gain, effective interest.
Modification - Creditor: Impairment = CA - PV of future cash flows (discounted at ORIGINAL rate)
Debtor uses total cash payments (undiscounted). Creditor uses PV (discounted at original rate).
